caption: The drawing depicts a framed sign with decorative wooden details. The frame is rectangular with wooden spindles on the sides and ornate scrolled elements at the top and bottom. At the top center, two symmetrical curved pieces are marked with the numbers "17" on the left and "92" on the right. The main section within the frame is a light tan or beige color with some shading to suggest texture. At the top of the sign, the letters "DR" are written in black, centered between two squiggly black lines. Below "DR," there is an image of a large bowl or vessel with floral decoration, containing red flowers with green stems and leaves and surrounded by yellow oval shapes. Underneath the bowl, the word “Entertainment” is written in a large, black script, with the bottom portion of the letters cut off such that only "Entertainme" is visible. The drawing uses primarily earth tones such as browns, reds, yellows, and greens, with dark outlines to emphasize the shape and features of each object. The entire composition is set against a plain, off-white background.
title: David Reed's Tavern Sign (recto)
